transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-12
Time: 10:00 - 10:58 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jonah Kim, Maya Patel, Leah Ortiz, Carlos Mendes, Priya Shah (plus a few observers)

Summary:
Quick sync to validate readiness for the Shipping Scheduler rollout, review the December scheduler incident (OOM / scheduling race), and align on gating criteria, canary plan, and rollback mechanisms. Action items captured at the end.

Topics:
- December scheduler outage postmortem highlights
- Rollout gating matrix (SLOs, error budget, perf regressions)
- Canary and staging configuration (node pools, batch sizes)
- Kernel fallback and quantization interactions
- Communication and customer-facing playbook

Transcript:
[00:00] Jonah: alright everyone, thanks for joining. I want to keep this tight — 45-ish minutes of sync then wrap. main goal is to get sign-off for the shipping scheduler rollout and make sure the incident followup items are closed. Maya, quick context?
[00:31] Maya: yeah, thanks. the PM side is that we have the scheduler feature implemented in ded-branch, the perf numbers look OK in unit tests, but the dec incident highlighted a pacing/race where large KV cache priming plus big batches caused OOMs on some nodes. we need a conservative rollout plan.
[01:05] Leah: to add, the outage had two levers: memory amplification from prefetch + our continuous batching heuristics converging. the scheduler made scheduling decisions that paired high-preload requests with high-batch workers. not a single bug, more of a workload-characteristic alignment issue.
[01:42] Carlos: yep and a small correction — the kernel fallback was hit but then didn't fully restore because the fallback flags didn't flow to the runtime in time. there was a control-plane race where the node labels updated slower than the job assignment.
[02:10] Jonah: right. that's why Carlos you and Leah had that emergency patch. shareable timeline would be great.
[02:30] Maya: I pasted a short timeline in the chat — it's not the full postmortem yet. but for rollout we want a three-phase plan: alpha (internal), staging canary, gradual prod ramp with capacity reservations. gating criteria are SLO delta < 2%, <0.5% error increase, and tail latency P99 within 1.2x baseline.
[03:05] Leah: those numbers are reasonable but we should include memory guardrails per node — e.g., limit prefix cache to 60% of allocatable and early OOM kill thresholds. and add a synthetic burst that mirrors the worst-case replay from Dec.
[03:40] Jonah: agreed. Priya — can you call out comms requirements? we need a customer-facing note and an internal incident page template.
[03:56] Priya: yes — I can draft both. we'll follow the standard incident template but include a clear rollback note and expected ETA if triggered. also we should mark which accounts get proactive outreach if error budget is hit — enterprise customers with dedicated pools first.
[04:25] Maya: also want to highlight the feature flag plan. defaults off for existing customers. we flip flag in dedicated pools only during canary, then through SLO checks roll to shared pools.
[04:45] Speaker 5: (background) can we be explicit about the canary size?
[04:50] Leah: propose a 3-node canary in staging with autoscaling disabled and a fixed batch-size seed so we can reproduce. run two 10-minute bursts and two sustained 20-minute loads.
[05:18] Carlos: and instrument the kernel fallback logs so they're captured at DEBUG and shipped to traces quickly. last time those logs were sparse.
[05:40] Jonah: ok — tradeoff discussion: performance vs safety. fallback paths reduce tail perf but prevent OOM. what's acceptable?
[05:55] Maya: prefer safety for GA but document perf delta and tied per-account opt-in for aggressive mode.
[06:12] Leah: we also examined quantization interactions in the postmortem. reduced precision increases cache density but can raise transient memory usage during kernel transitions. need to verify that in staging.
[06:40] Jonah: good note. any blocker on that? Carlos?
[06:46] Carlos: I have a prototype of a kernel-selection shim that can pre-reserve kv cache allocations during transitions to avoid spikes. it's untested at scale but I'll baseline it in staging.
[07:08] Maya: ok, let's map out the gating matrix now. first gate: alpha success — internal infra + internal teams usage for one week with no tail regression. second gate: staging canary success — pass automated SLO checks and synthetic burst. third gate: gradual prod with reserved capacity and 24h observation.
[07:45] Leah: what about rollback? how quick can we flip flags and return? we need an automated fallback that can revert scheduler decisions per pool.
[08:00] Carlos: we already have per-pool feature flags. the missing piece is an automated rollback orchestrator that can detect SLO breach and flip flags then drain affected nodes. I can mock a runbook.
[08:20] Jonah: good. action item for Carlos to produce runbook and a command example for immediate rollback.
[08:35] Maya: I'll add that to the checklist.
[08:40] Speaker 2: (inaudible) ask if we can limit batch size per request at scheduler level?
[08:48] Leah: yes we can impose soft caps and circuit-break on batch growth. it's a quick mitigation and should be included in alpha.
[09:05] Jonah: moving on to the incident timeline review — Leah can you walk through the key events from Dec 14th?
[09:12] Leah: sure. roughly: 11:03 UTC spike in preloads from a customer replay job; 11:05 continuous batching heuristics aggregated into ~6 nodes, 11:07 memory pressure hit on node-42, OOM killer started evicting, 11:09 scheduler retried assignments and pushed more work onto the remaining nodes; 11:14 control plane applied a 'fallback kernel' but the node labelling race meant new jobs still landed on hot nodes. the system stabilized around 11:23 after manual intervention.
[09:58] Maya: were there any alerts that should have pre-empted this?
[10:03] Leah: we had host-level memory alerts, but the alerting thresholds were set too high for the cache-mem pattern. I recommend adding a 'KV cache priming ahead' alert at 70% of cache allocation.
[10:25] Carlos: also, the tracing spans for kernel transitions were sampled low and the logs were truncated; we need higher sampling for the next two weeks post-rollout.
[10:40] Jonah: sampling up for kernel spans only, agreed. Priya, can you own comms for that elevated trace retention?
[10:48] Priya: yep — I'll coordinate with Trust & Safety and infra billing to accept the temporary cost.
[11:05] Speaker 3: (off) how much perf regression did we see with fallback? numbers?
[11:10] Leah: around 10-18% P99 regression in some cases, average 6% across the mixed workloads. detailed numbers in the postmortem doc.
[11:26] Jonah: that's significant but tolerable for a safety-first rollout. we need to mark accounts that cannot tolerate that as opt-out.
[11:40] Maya: next, test plan. Carlos will run kernel shim baseline, Leah will run synthetic workloads, Maya will run cross-account canary, and Priya will prep comms.
[12:00] Carlos: timeline I'm thinking — baseline and shim tests by 1/15, canary in staging 1/16-1/17, roll to prod 1/20 if all good.
[12:20] Jonah: that seems aggressive but doable if we keep scope tight.
[12:30] Speaker 4: any outstanding dependencies on Dedicated or Private infra?
[12:36] Carlos: Dedicated pools need a small change in the autoscaler config to avoid preemption; we have a PR that needs review.
[12:48] Leah: also, we need to ensure the KMS keys for logging in private deployments are accessible for the new debug traces.
[13:05] Maya: let's talk about checklist items — I'll call them out and we can confirm owners.
[13:12] Maya: 1) update rollout checklist with SLO gating (owner: Maya) — done, pending review. 2) canary staging runbook (owner: Leah) — in progress. 3) kernel fallback examples and shim tests (owner: Carlos) — in progress. 4) comms templates and customer outreach list (owner: Priya) — pending.
[13:50] Jonah: add 5) increase kernel transition span sampling for next 2 weeks (owner: Leah) and 6) automated rollback orchestrator runbook (owner: Carlos).
[14:10] Leah: note that the synthetic burst harness needs a small tweak: align sequence length distribution to real traffic peaks — I have a script that does that but it's in a private branch.
[14:30] Carlos: can you share that branch?
[14:32] Leah: yes, will open PR after tests.
[14:45] Speaker 2: small tangent — will this change affect token pricing estimates for committed customers?
[14:52] Maya: shouldn't materially change token cost, but we may see short-term cost upticks due to elevated trace retention and canary reserved capacity. we'll track and notify finance.
[15:12] Jonah: great. let's spend 10 minutes on risk review — what could go wrong and how to mitigate quickly.
[15:20] Leah: risk: undetected memory amplification with new customer replays. mitigations: early cache caps, burst alarms, and emergency OOM proxies that redirect traffic.
[15:40] Carlos: risk: control-plane lag causing mismatch between flag state and job assignment. mitigation: add optimistic checks at assignment time and fallback to safe nodes.
[16:00] Maya: risk: customer impact for enterprise shared pools. mitigation: run the canary only on dedicated pools initially and provide opt-in for shared beta customers.
[16:20] Jonah: sounds good. any legal/compliance flags?
[16:24] Priya: no new compliance risks beyond elevated traces; we've vetted retention with security.
[16:32] Jonah: ok last section — launch gating sign-off. read the checklist: alpha internal pass, staging canary pass with two burst runs, kernel shim baseline, comms ready, and rollback runbook. thumbs?
[16:50] Maya: thumbs up from product.
[16:55] Leah: thumbs from SRE contingent but conditional on the two synthetic bursts passing.
[17:05] Carlos: engineering thumbs provided shim tests pass in staging.
[17:12] Jonah: I'll take executive signoff pending the items we just discussed. I'll schedule a quick follow-up on 1/14 to confirm go/no-go.
[17:25] Maya: final ask — please document the flame graph artifacts that were useful in the postmortem so others can run them easily.
[17:35] Leah: will do and add links to the postmortem doc.
[17:45] Jonah: cool. any other items?
[17:50] Speaker 6: (quiet) can you share the script for the synthetic burst?
[17:54] Leah: attached in the chat, will PR.
[18:00] Jonah: ok let's recap quick: action items assigned (see chat and metadata). we run canary in staging 1/16, baseline shim tests by 1/15, and aim for prod roll on 1/20 pending checks. I'll book the 1/14 exec decision slot. thanks all.
[18:25] Maya: thanks everyone.
[18:30] meeting ends
